correctness.rationale: For fixed \(R>0\), the radial \(p\)-capacity is \(I_\varepsilon(R)^{1-p}\) with \(I_\varepsilon(R)=\int_R^\infty S(t)^{-\varepsilon}dt\) and \(\varepsilon=(p-1)^{-1}\). The relative \(O(t^{-1})\) error contributes \(o(\varepsilon)\) to \(h\varepsilon I_\varepsilon\); \(\Gamma(1-k\varepsilon,h\varepsilon R)=1+k\gamma_{\mathrm E}\varepsilon-hR\varepsilon+o(\varepsilon)\). Taking the reciprocal and applying the dimension normalization yields exactly the stated coefficient. The theorem is restricted to the explicit sphere-area asymptotic and fixed radius.

Under a precise sphere-growth law, this coefficient separates the scale-invariant amplitude \(C h^{m-1-k}\) and the radius term \(hR\), distinguishing models with the same exponential rate and polynomial exponent. It is an exact, reusable next-order benchmark for geometric potential theory.
